title: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Overloaded Operators
sourceFile: Overloaded Operators - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on Overloaded Operators in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which of the following keyword is used to overload user defined types by defining static member functions?

options.text: op
opoverload
operator
operatoroverload

questions.explanation: User-defined operators are declared as public static methods named with the operator keyword, for example public static Vector operator +(Vector a, Vector b).

questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct in nature?

options.text: The conditional logical operators cannot be overloaded
The array indexing operator can be overloaded
A public or nested public preference type does not overload the equality operator
None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: && and || cannot be overloaded directly (they use true/false and &/|). [] is not overloaded as an operator; you write an indexer. Option c is garbled ("preference type"). A type may overload == and !=.

questions.question: Arrange the following overloaded operators in increasing order of precedence?
questions.explanation: Among these operators, & has the lowest precedence, then shift <<, then additive +, then multiplicative % and / (same level). Overloading does not change precedence.

questions.question: Operators that can be overloaded are?
questions.explanation: + can be overloaded. || cannot. Compound assignment += is not declared separately; it uses the overloaded +. [] is provided by an indexer, not operator [].

questions.question: Which statements are correct about operator overloading?

options.text: Mathematical or physical modeling where we use classes to represent objects such as vectors, matrices, complex-numbers etc
Graphical programs where coordinate related objects are used to represent positions on the screen
Financial programs where a class represents an amount of money
All of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Those are typical uses of overloaded operators: types that behave like numbers, vectors, points, or money can use + - * and similar so expressions stay readable.

questions.question: Correct way to define operator method or to perform operator overloading is?

options.text: All of the mentioned

questions.explanation: The form is public static ReturnType operator +(T a, T b). The operator token must appear before the operator symbol.

questions.question: Correct method to define + operator is?

options.text: public sample operator +(int a, int b)
public abstract operator +(int a, int b)
public static sample operator +(int a, int b)
public abstract sample operator +(int a, int b)

questions.explanation: Operators must be public and static (and not abstract). At least one parameter must be the enclosing type; overloading + for two ints inside sample would not compile unless a parameter is sample.

questions.question: Which of the following are common mistakes when overloading operators?

options.text: Forgetting to declare an operator method as public
Forgetting to declare an operator method as static
Forgetting to return a bool type value while overloading a relational operator
All of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Operator methods must be public static. Relational operators (== != < > <= >=) should return bool. The original question text did not say these were errors.

questions.question: In typical operator-overloading examples, what is Vector?

options.text: class
method()
a user-defined type (class or struct)
none of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Vector is not a built-in C# type here; it is a sample class or struct that overloads operators, e.g. public static Vector operator +(Vector a, Vector b). Calling it only a "data type" is vague; it is a user-defined type.

questions.question: Choose the wrong statement from the given set of statements?

options.text: All operators in C#.NET cannot be overloaded
We can use the new modifier to modify a nested type if the nested type is hiding another type
Operator overloading permits the use of symbols to represent computations for a type
In case of operator overloading all parameters must be of different type than the class or struct that declares the operators

questions.explanation: d is false: at least one operand must be the enclosing type. a is awkwardly phrased but means not every operator can be overloaded, which is true. b and c are true.
